# Auto-Generated Reports

> ⚠️ **DO NOT MANUALLY EDIT FILES IN THIS FOLDER**

This folder contains **auto-generated reports** that are created by running test commands. Any manual edits will be lost the next time the reports are regenerated.

## Files in This Folder

| File | Generated By | Purpose |
|------|-------------|---------|
| [LICENSE_COMPLIANCE.md](LICENSE_COMPLIANCE.md) | `dotnet run --project tests/SysDocs.Tests -- --license-compliance` | Complete list of NuGet dependencies with their licenses |
| [TEST_TRACEABILITY.md](TEST_TRACEABILITY.md) | `dotnet run --project tests/SysDocs.Tests -- --traceability` | Requirement-to-test mapping with coverage statistics |

## How to Use

### View Current Data
```bash
# Always regenerate first to get latest data
cd /path/to/SysDocs

# Generate license report
dotnet run --project tests/SysDocs.Tests -- --license-compliance

# Generate traceability report
dotnet run --project tests/SysDocs.Tests -- --traceability

# Then view the files
cat reports/LICENSE_COMPLIANCE.md
cat reports/TEST_TRACEABILITY.md
```

### When to Regenerate

- **LICENSE_COMPLIANCE.md**: After adding/removing/updating NuGet packages
- **TEST_TRACEABILITY.md**: After adding/removing tests or requirements

### Version Control

**These files SHOULD be committed to git** so reviewers can see:
- What dependencies changed
- What test coverage changed
- What requirements are now covered

### For Policy and Procedures

Auto-generated reports contain **data only**. For policies, procedures, and guides, see:

- [../docs/LICENSE_COMPLIANCE_SUMMARY.md](../docs/LICENSE_COMPLIANCE_SUMMARY.md) - License policy, approved licenses, audit schedule
- [../docs/VV_SETUP_SUMMARY.md](../docs/VV_SETUP_SUMMARY.md) - V&V system usage guide
- [../VERIFICATION_VALIDATION.md](../VERIFICATION_VALIDATION.md) - V&V strategy
- [../REQUIREMENTS.md](../REQUIREMENTS.md) - System requirements

## Architecture Decision

**Why separate `reports/` from `docs/`?**

1. **Clear ownership**: Machine-generated vs human-written
2. **Prevents accidents**: Obvious that these files shouldn't be manually edited
3. **Better organization**: Data in `reports/`, procedures in `docs/`
4. **Easy to regenerate**: `rm -rf reports/ && regenerate-all`
5. **Visual separation**: Easier to see what's what in file listings
